subject: Walk mode: the view out of the windows
decision: Walk mode draws, outside the glass, the same city context massing as /towers (context.glb, P-064), the same gradient sky and daylight (P-063), and both towers as their cited plan outline (data/geometry-params.json plate parameters) extruded to each tower's cited roof elevation from the manifest, with no facade detail. The group is shifted so this floor's plate sits at the scene origin: the tower's plan centre moves to minus its layout position (P-066) and the ground drops by this floor's cited elevation above the floor 1 (Concourse) line, which is y = 0 in the tower files and the ground the context is extruded from (P-067). This tower's outline is cut out between the underside of this floor's slab and the top of the slab above, so the floor the visitor stands on is the cited plate, core and columns already drawn. Fog starts nearer than in /towers (700 m against 1,800 m) because the eye is inside the plate and the far city should soften. Nothing outside is pickable and nothing carries a name. A floor with no cited elevation in the manifest draws no outside at all rather than guessing a height.
reasoning: Chris's feedback (2026-09-11): from a high floor you should see the city below. Everything used is already cited for /towers; reusing the same files and the same layout choice keeps the two views consistent and adds no new claim. Rejected: loading the full tower .glb files for the exterior (330,000 triangles of facade to draw one wall of, and z-fighting with the floor's own columns); a photographic skyline or satellite imagery (no 2001 imagery is cited, and modern imagery would show the wrong city); drawing the other tower's facade windows (window width is unresolved, towers.window_width); applying a ground elevation (P-067 keeps the context at y = 0); inventing a height for a floor whose elevation is not in the manifest.

subject: Walk mode: colour in the illustration layer
decision: The illustration layer's carpet is now one tile-textured sheet per tenant zone in that zone's industry colour, at 60% opacity over the cited zone tint, 35% for a reported row, and 20% in the pale no-record tone for a zone with no tenant row, so the evidence scale still reads through the carpet. Each partition carries a 6 cm strip along its top in the zone colour, set per instance. The ceiling grid lines and tiles are lighter than before. Plaques, signs, desks, chairs and partitions keep their stipple and white treatments. The colour is borrowed from the industry palette (lib/industry-colors.ts) but through separate materials: the illustration layer still shares no material with the cited layer.
reasoning: Chris's feedback (2026-09-11): the walking view had no colour and read as rows of desks. Tinting by the zone's industry colour makes a zone read as one workplace without any furnishing claiming to be evidence, and the illustration label stays on. Rejected: per-tenant colour schemes or logos (would present a specific tenant's fit-out, which is uncited); colouring the desks or partitions themselves (would make the furniture read as a finish rather than a drawing convention); a stronger carpet over a no-record zone (would suggest occupancy the source does not give).

subject: Walk mode: figures in the illustration layer
decision: Stylised figures are added to the illustration layer: three capsules and a sphere each (legs, body, head), about 1.75 m tall, no face, no name, no employer, in one of three muted clothing tones with one leg tone and one head tone for all. Per tenant zone with at least one illustration desk: one figure per eight desks, at least one and at most six, at most 48 on a floor, and none in a zone with no tenant row. The first figure in a zone stands a step in front of the zone's plaque facing the core; the rest walk slow loops (0.9 m/s) along the two aisles the fit-out leaves free, inside the glass and around the core, clear of the zone boundary walls, and never leave their zone. Motion is updated on a 20 frames per second budget. The figures mount inside the illustration group, so the layer toggle removes them, and the persistent label is widened to 'Illustration. Furnishings and figures are not a reconstruction.' Desks are no longer placed within 1.7 m of a plaque, so the plaque can be read and the figure can stand at it.
reasoning: Chris's feedback (2026-09-11): a working floor should have people moving around. Figures with no identity and a fixed count rule show occupancy without asserting who worked where or how many; the counts are a rendering choice, not a headcount. Rejected: figures in no-record zones (would suggest occupancy the source does not give); more figures on a floor with more listed square feet (would read as a headcount claim); animated character models or motion capture (uncited, and heavier than the budget allows); faces, name tags or uniforms; a count rule based on the cited occupant load of 390 per floor (that figure is the code capacity used to size the stairs, not an occupancy).

subject: Walk mode: wayfinding signs on the core faces
decision: Each numbered floor carries an Elevators sign on each of the four core faces and one Stairs sign beside the north-face sign, at 2.05 m, drawn as cited-layer cards in the plaque style. The Elevators sign gives the local elevator count for the zone (towers.local_elevators_per_zone), the zone's floor range (interpretive, P-072), the sky lobby and express count for the zone (towers.express_elevators_concourse_to_44 or _78), and the tower total (towers.elevators_total), and says that shaft positions are not cited and the sign marks the core face, not a bank. The Stairs sign gives the count and widths (towers.stairways_per_tower, towers.stair_a_c_width, towers.stair_b_width) and the cited location (towers.stairs_location), and says the position on this floor is not cited. Sign placement is a presentation choice; the parameter ids are printed on each sign.
reasoning: Chris's feedback (2026-09-11): a floor should have signs pointing to the elevators and stairs. Every figure on the signs is already cited for the elevator panel; putting them on the core face answers the wayfinding question without drawing a bank or a door. Rejected: arrows to a specific bank position (unresolved towers.elevator_shaft_positions_in_core); a stair door on a specific face (no position is cited); period signage styling (no sign is cited); signs on the lobby, which has its own cited statements and plaques (P-074).
